NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B is a vision language model built on the
Nemotron-H hybrid Mamba-2 and Transformer architecture with a RADIO vision
encoder. It accepts text, image, and video input and returns text; it does not
accept audio input. Refer to the [Support Matrix for NIMs](https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/large-language-models/2.0.13/reference/support-matrix) for supported profiles and GPUs.

The inference backend is vLLM 0.31.0.

**What NIM configures for you.** Each packaged profile carries the full set of
engine arguments validated for its GPU and precision: tensor parallelism,
context length (up to 1,048,576 tokens), Mamba cache settings, the
`nemotron_v3` reasoning parser, the `qwen3_coder` tool-call parser, the chat
template, video decoding, and speculative decoding (the built-in MTP head on
all profiles except NVIDIA A100, which runs without speculative decoding). BF16 profiles
also enable LoRA adapter serving. You do not need to pass engine flags through
`NIM_PASSTHROUGH_ARGS`. Overriding `NIM_PASSTHROUGH_ARGS` replaces the packaged
chat-template argument, so only set it when you intend to change engine
behavior.

The token-in/token-out endpoint `/inference/v1/generate` and the render
endpoints `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/completions/render` are not
served by default and return 404. To enable them, start the container with
`--enable-scale-out` and keep the packaged chat template:

## Known Issues

This release includes the following known issues and limitations:

- **Select the profile explicitly.** Automatic profile selection does not
filter on GPU model or per-GPU memory, so on some systems it can pick a
profile packaged for a different GPU. List the profiles in the container and
set `NIM_MODEL_PROFILE` to the one that matches your GPU, as shown in
[How to Choose the Right Model Profile](https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/large-language-models/2.0.13/get-started/advanced/get-started-nemotron-3.5-super-vl#how-to-choose-the-right-model-profile).
- **Video requests can run out of `max_tokens` while reasoning.** With
reasoning on, the model can spend more than 2,048 tokens reasoning about a
video before it writes the answer; the response then ends with
`finish_reason: "length"` and empty `content`. Set `max_tokens` to 8192 or
higher for video requests, or turn reasoning off for the request with
`"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}`.
- **`thinking_token_budget` leaves `content` empty when the budget is**
**reached.** Control reasoning with `reasoning_effort` or `enable_thinking`
instead, as described in [Control Reasoning](https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/large-language-models/2.0.13/get-started/advanced/get-started-nemotron-3.5-super-vl#control-reasoning).
- **Forced tool choice returns arguments for tools that take none.** When a
tool’s `parameters` declare no properties (`"properties": {}`) and the
request forces the call with `"tool_choice": "required"` or a named function,
the returned `arguments` can contain invented keys instead of `{}`, and
frameworks that validate arguments reject the call before running the tool.
This comes from vLLM. For tools without parameters, use
`"tool_choice": "auto"`, which returns `{}`.
- **`json_object` output can omit the fields you ask for.**`"response_format": {"type": "json_object"}` guarantees valid JSON, not a
particular shape; the model can return `{}` or leave out a requested field.
When the response must contain specific fields, use
`"response_format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}` with those fields listed as
`required`.

## Prerequisites

Before deploying a NIM LLM and VLM container, ensure your environment
meets the following requirements:

### Hardware Requirements

### Model Cache

NIM downloads model weights to a cache on the host that you mount into the container. Artifacts persist across restarts, so you do not pull the full model on every run.

#### Local Cache

An essential variable to configure on your host system is the cache path directory. This directory is mapped from the host machine to container; assets (for example, model weights) are downloaded to this host directory and persist across container restarts. Configuring a local cache is highly recommended, as it avoids re-downloading large model files upon subsequent container restarts. You can name the environment variable containing the path to the local cache whatever you want.

Create the cache directory and export an environment variable:

```

```

When you start the NIM container, you must map your host machine’s local cache directory (`$LOCAL_NIM_CACHE`) to the container’s internal cache path (`/opt/nim/.cache`) using a Docker volume mount, such as `-v "$LOCAL_NIM_CACHE:/opt/nim/.cache"`. This mapping ensures that the large model weights downloaded by the container are saved to your host machine. Because containers are ephemeral, any data stored only inside the container is lost when it stops. By using a volume mount, subsequent container runs detect the existing model files in your local cache and skip the lengthy download process, allowing the NIM to start up faster.

#### Cache Directory Permissions

The NIM container runs as a non-root user with GID 0 (root group). The cache directory on your host must be writable by GID 0:

Without it, the container will fail with `PermissionError` when writing to
cache, config, or log paths.

To make this setting permanent across terminal sessions, you can add `export LOCAL_NIM_CACHE=~/.cache/nim` to your `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc` profile.

You can serve a fine-tuned checkpoint (for example, after SFT) with this NIM and

# NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4

[![Pre-Training Datasets](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%97%84%EF%B8%8F_Pre--Training_Datasets-Available_Here-76B900?logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/nemotron-pre-training-datasets)[![Homepage](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%8F%A0Nemotron%20Developer%20Page-Learn%20More%20Here!-536af5?color=76B900&logoColor=white)](https://developer.nvidia.com/nemotron)[![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%93%9DPaper-Read%20Now!-536af5?color=76B900&logoColor=white)](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/files/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-and-Lightning-Technical-Report.pdf)[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-NVIDIA%20AI%20Developer-7289da?logo=discord&logoColor=white&color=7289da)](https://discord.gg/9xpKQtVvrk)

[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-OpenMDW--1.1-f5de53)](https://openmdw.ai/license/1-1/)

[![image](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4/resolve/main/accuracy_plot.png)](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4/blob/main/accuracy_plot.png)

## Description

**NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4** is the quantized release of NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a vision-language model for reasoning, coding, tool use, document understanding, and video understanding. It uses NVFP4 quantization to reduce memory requirements, with quantization-aware distillation from the [BF16 model](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16).

The model combines interleaved Mamba-2, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), and attention layers with a C-RADIO vision encoder and a vision-language connector. It has **120B total parameters** and **12B active parameters** and supports context lengths up to **1M tokens**. Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) enables native speculative decoding.

This model is ready for commercial or non-commercial use.

## Model Summary

|  |  |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Total Parameters** | 120B (12B active) |
| **Architecture** | Mamba-2–Transformer hybrid Mixture of Experts with a C-RADIO vision encoder |
| **Precision** | NVFP4 (mixed-precision quantized weights) |
| **Context Length** | Up to 1M tokens; deployment settings are listed below |
| **Inputs / Outputs** | Text, images, and video / text |
| **Deployment** | 1× DGX Spark, 1x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000, 1× H200, 2× H100, or 1× GB200 |
| **Speculative Decoding** | Native Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) |
| **Reasoning Mode** | Configurable through the chat template (`enable_thinking=True/False`) |
| **Recommended Sampling** | Text: temperature 1.0, top\_p 0.95; vision: temperature 0.6, top\_p 0.95 |
| **Best For** | Efficient deployment of text and vision-language agents |
| **License** | [OpenMDW-1.1](https://openmdw.ai/license/1-1/) |

## Model Overview

**Model Developer:** NVIDIA Corporation

### What is Nemotron?

NVIDIA Nemotron™ is a family of open models with open weights, training data, and recipes, delivering leading efficiency and accuracy for building specialized AI agents.

## Quick Start

This vLLM configuration is intended for **DGX Spark (GB10) only**. It serves the model with one concurrent sequence and seven speculative tokens per draft using [LiLiCorr](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4-LiLiCorr).

> Nemotron 3.5 Super VL has configurable reasoning levels: `off`, `on (medium)`, and `on`. Selecting `on (medium)` will reduce the number of tokens generated compared to `on`, but may impact accuracy. You can learn about the reasoning budget [here](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4#text-and-reasoning)!

Use Docker with NVIDIA GPU support and the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-cf5cea2da37d3dfed27d2e0aa3041c3e553c2d57` image. If the model requires authentication, set `HF_TOKEN` in your shell before launching the container.

```bash
export MODEL=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4
export DRAFT_MODEL=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4-LiLiCorr
```

```bash
vllm serve $MODEL \
  --served-model-name nemotron-3.5-super-vl \
  --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --speculative_config.model $DRAFT_MODEL\
  --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens 7 \
  --speculative_config.method dflash \
  --mamba-backend flashinfer \
  --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
  --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding \
  --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 \
  --enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint \
  --video-pruning-rate 0.5 \
  --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"fps": 2, "num_frames": 256}}' \
  --block-size 64 \
  --prefix-match-unit 64 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3
```

Wait for the server to finish loading the model and compiling kernels, then check the endpoint:

```bash
curl --fail http://localhost:8000/v1/models
```

## Model Architecture

- **Architecture Type:** Mamba-2–Transformer hybrid Mixture of Experts (MoE) with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP)
- **Network Architecture:** Nemotron Hybrid MoE with 512 routed experts per MoE layer, a C-RADIO vision encoder, and a vision-language connector
- **Number of Model Parameters:** 120B total / 12B active

## Model Design

The model combines sparse expert computation, attention, and Mamba-2 layers to support long-context processing. The vision encoder and connector turn visual inputs into representations processed by the language backbone. A shared MTP head predicts future tokens recursively for speculative decoding.

The model supports up to 1M tokens of context. The prompt, visual inputs, conversation history, tool results, and generated response share this context window. Individual deployment recipes may use a smaller context window to accommodate the available GPU memory and concurrency.

## Training Methodology

**Stage 1: Foundation and Multi-Token Prediction**

The language backbone is initialized from Nemotron 3 Super Base. A shared MTP head is trained for 100B tokens while the backbone remains frozen, followed by 1T tokens of distillation from Nemotron 3 Ultra Base.

**Stage 2: Continued Pre-Training and Mid-Training**

The model undergoes 100B tokens of Indic continued pre-training, a 35B-token extension to 1M context, 67B tokens of software-engineering mid-training at 256K context, and a final 9B-token long-context recovery stage. Software-engineering data includes repositories, issue–pull-request pairs, commit diffs, build and CI logs, and agent trajectories.

**Stage 3: Vision-Language Training**

A C-RADIO vision encoder and connector extend the language backbone to visual inputs, including images, document pages, and video frames.

**Stage 4: Supervised Fine-Tuning**

A two-stage supervised fine-tuning pipeline jointly trains the language and vision components on vision, reasoning, code, tools, chat, safety, and long-context data. Training uses packed sequences of up to 524,288 tokens.

**Stage 5: Reinforcement Learning and Distillation**

Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, reinforcement learning from human feedback, and specialized teacher training improve reasoning, agentic, chat, and vision capabilities. Multi-teacher on-policy distillation consolidates these capabilities into a single model.

**Stage 6: MTP Boosting**

The MTP head is further trained against the frozen post-trained backbone to improve speculative-decoding acceptance.

**Stage 7: Quantization and Quantization-Aware Distillation**

The model is quantized with [NVIDIA Model Optimizer](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer) and refined through quantization-aware distillation using the supervised fine-tuning data blend. The vision encoder, connector, Mamba convolutions, and embeddings remain in BF16, and the MoE router remains in FP32. Inference uses W4A4 on Blackwell and W4A16 on non-Blackwell platforms, according to the serving configuration.

### Speculative Decoding

The serving examples enable the model's native MTP head. No separate drafter download is required for these vLLM and SGLang recipes leveraging MTP. In vLLM, `num_speculative_tokens` controls draft length; in SGLang, the MTP draft length uses `--speculative-num-steps` to config.

For DGX Spark, we also provide a [LiLiCorr](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4-LiLiCorr) speculative drafter, which accelerates decoding by drafting multiple future tokens in parallel and using a lightweight correlation head to select compatible candidates across adjacent positions. Nemotron Super 3.5 VL verifies the proposed block, allowing generation to advance by multiple accepted tokens per verification step while preserving the target model's output distribution with correct speculative verification. It is recommended to use LiLiCorr for DGX Spark deployments in all scenarios.

Performance depends on hardware, request length, and concurrency. To compare with standard decoding, remove the speculative configuration while keeping the model, workload, sampling parameters, and other server settings the same.

#### Tool calling

The model requests a tool call; the application executes it and returns the result. This complete example uses a local inventory lookup.

```python
import json
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")
model = "nemotron-3.5-super-vl"
inventory = {"keyboard": 12, "monitor": 5}
tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {\
    "name": "get_inventory",\
    "description": "Return the inventory count for a product.",\
    "parameters": {\
        "type": "object",\
        "properties": {"product": {"type": "string", "enum": ["keyboard", "monitor"]}},\
        "required": ["product"],\
        "additionalProperties": False,\
    },\
}}]
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "How many keyboards are in stock?"}]

def complete(history, tool_choice="auto"):
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=model,
        messages=history,
        tools=tools,
        tool_choice=tool_choice,
        temperature=1.0,
        top_p=0.95,
        max_tokens=16384,
        extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True}},
    )
    choice = response.choices[0]
    if choice.finish_reason == "length":
        raise RuntimeError("The response was truncated; increase max_tokens.")
    return choice.message

message = complete(messages)
messages.append(message.model_dump(exclude_none=True))
if not message.tool_calls:
    print(message.content)
else:
    for call in message.tool_calls:
        arguments = json.loads(call.function.arguments)
        if (call.function.name != "get_inventory"
                or not isinstance(arguments, dict)
                or set(arguments) != {"product"}
                or not isinstance(arguments["product"], str)
                or arguments["product"] not in inventory):
            raise ValueError("Invalid inventory tool call")
        product = arguments["product"]
        messages.append({
            "role": "tool",
            "tool_call_id": call.id,
            "content": json.dumps({"product": product, "count": inventory[product]}),
        })
```

### **Crawled and Scraped from Online Sources by NVIDIA**

The English Common Crawl data was downloaded from the Common Crawl Foundation (see their FAQ for details on their crawling) and includes the snapshots CC-MAIN-2013-20 through CC-MAIN-2025-13. The data was subsequently deduplicated and filtered in various ways used in the Nemotron-CC data pipeline. Additionally, we extracted data for fifteen languages from the following three Common Crawl snapshots: CC-MAIN-2024-51, CC-MAIN-2025-08, CC-MAIN-2025-18. The fifteen languages included were Arabic, Chinese, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, and Thai. As we did not have reliable multilingual model-based quality classifiers available, we applied just heuristic filtering instead—similar to what we did for lower quality English data in the Nemotron-CC pipeline, but selectively removing some filters for some languages that did not work well. Deduplication was done in the same way as for Nemotron-CC.

The GitHub Crawl was collected using the GitHub REST API and the Amazon S3 API. Each crawl was operated in accordance with the rate limits set by its respective source, either GitHub or S3. We collect raw source code and subsequently remove any having a license which does not exist in our permissive-license set.

NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B is a **120B parameter, 12B active** hybrid reasoning MoE model with **up to 1M tokens of context**. It accepts text, images and video for document understanding, computer use and agent workflows, and generates text.

It supports JSON output and tool calling, and includes a built-in Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) head. Unsloth GGUFs range from **46.1GB (1-bit) to 132GB (8-bit)**. We also made NVFP4 quants (79GB) and added the LiLiCorr DSpark module. **Unsloth quants:** [NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-GGUF)

[Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL Guide](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/nemotron-3.5-super-vl#run-nemotron-35-super-vl-guide) [Run Nemotron-3.5-Bolt Guide](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/nemotron-3.5-bolt)

### ⚙️ Usage Guide[Direct link to heading](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/nemotron-3.5-super-vl\#usage-guide)

**Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Requirements**

The smallest **1-bit GGUF is 46.1GB**; plan for at least **64GB of RAM or unified memory**. The **4-bit GGUF is 86.9GB**, with around **128GB** recommended. You can also split the model across system RAM and GPU VRAM. You can also run the NVFP4 which is a direct lossless conversion from NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-NVFP4.

Memory figures are **planning estimates** for a modest context, including headroom for the operating system, runtime, KV cache and vision projector. GGUF file size alone is not the RAM requirement. Longer contexts and video need more memory; all model weights must be stored even though only 12B parameters are active per token. Count unified memory once.

A **128GB unified-memory system**, such as DGX Spark, fits the suggested 4-bit memory budget. NVIDIA documents DGX Spark support through NIM; these GGUF memory estimates are not measured performance results.

### Recommended Settings[Direct link to heading](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/nemotron-3.5-super-vl\#recommended-settings)

NVIDIA recommends these settings:

Parameter

Start with **16K context** and increase it as memory allows. The model supports up to **1M tokens**, but your runtime or NIM profile may have a lower limit. Prompt and output tokens share this budget. The examples serve one request at a time.

**Thinking on or off**

The model supports `enable_thinking=True` (default) for reasoning and `enable_thinking=False` for direct answers. NVIDIA NIM accepts this through chat-template kwargs. For local GGUFs, use the model’s chat template and your runtime’s supported thinking controls.

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL ships with **MTP (Multi-Token Prediction)**, which is enabled by default in Unsloth for faster output. You can turn it off in the settings. See our [MTP guide](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/mtp).

Go to [Unsloth Chat](https://unsloth.ai/docs/new/studio/chat) or Model hub and search for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL in the search bar and download your desired model and quant. Now you're ready to run the model!

Inference parameters should be auto-set when using Unsloth, however you can still change it manually. You can also edit the context length, chat template and other settings.

To try image understanding, attach a PNG or JPEG and ask **“What is this image?”**

For more information, you can view our [Unsloth inference guide](https://unsloth.ai/docs/new/studio/chat).

3

#### Serve Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with Unsloth API[Direct link to heading](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/nemotron-3.5-super-vl\#serve-nemotron-3.5-super-vl-with-unsloth-api)

Serve Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with `unsloth run`. You can pass llama-server flags for context size, GPU layers and other settings. See our [API docs](https://unsloth.ai/docs/basics/api) or [unsloth start](https://unsloth.ai/docs/integrations/unsloth-start).

```
unsloth run --model unsloth/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-GGUF:UD-IQ2_XXS \
    --ctx-size 4096 --parallel 1 --alias nemotron-super-vl \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001
```

### KLD Benchmarks[Direct link to heading](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/nemotron-3.5-super-vl\#kld-benchmarks)

We used UD-3 to convert Nemotron Super and did general KLD and also an unseen text KLD dataset to gauge for overfitting - generally UD-Q4\_K\_XL is the best in terms of KLD vs disk space - NVFP4 is also generally ok, and UD-Q3\_K\_XL is a also reasonable.

![](https://unsloth.ai/docs/~gitbook/image?url=https%3A%2F%2F3215535692-files.gitbook.io%2F%7E%2Ffiles%2Fv0%2Fb%2Fgitbook-x-prod.appspot.com%2Fo%2Fspaces%252FxhOjnexMCB3dmuQFQ2Zq%252Fuploads%252FI0Lb9lHn00vouMw6Lj8n%252Fnemotron35_super_vl_kld_vs_disk%282%29.png%3Falt%3Dmedia%26token%3D7aea3a84-5740-45e3-b542-2982133cafdb&width=768&dpr=3&quality=100&sign=837685acd93cc06ebe41b735753f1281&sv=3)

#### 🦙 Run Nemotron 3.5 Super VL in llama.cpp[Direct link to heading](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/nemotron-3.5-super-vl\#run-nemotron-35-super-vl-in-llama.cpp)

1

**Build llama.cpp**

Install the latest version of llama.cpp. You can follow the build instructions below as well. Change `-DGGML_CUDA=ON` to `-DGGML_CUDA=OFF` if you don't have a GPU or just want CPU inference. **For Apple Mac / Metal devices**, set `-DGGML_CUDA=OFF` then continue as usual - Metal support is on by default.

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
apt-get update
apt-get install pciutils build-essential cmake curl libcurl4-openssl-dev -y
git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp
cmake llama.cpp -B llama.cpp/build \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_CUDA=ON
cmake --build llama.cpp/build --config Release -j --clean-first --target llama-cli llama-mtmd-cli llama-server llama-gguf-split
cp llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-* llama.cpp
```

Video needs both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` on your PATH. Continue the commands below from this `llama.cpp` directory.

2

**Download the Unsloth GGUF**

Download the model and its vision projector:

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -U huggingface_hub

hf download unsloth/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-GGUF \
    --local-dir models/nemotron-super-vl \
    --include "*UD-Q4_K_XL*.gguf" "*mmproj*.gguf"
```

Set the paths to the downloaded model and its matching projector. For a split GGUF, keep every shard together and point to the **first shard**. Adjust the filenames below to match your download.

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
MODEL_FILE="models/nemotron-super-vl/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf"
MMPROJ_FILE="models/nemotron-super-vl/mmproj-BF16.gguf"
```

3

**Run text and images**

For text:

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
./llama.cpp/llama-cli \
    --model "$MODEL_FILE" --ctx-size 16384 --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 0 --min-p 0.0 \
    --prompt "Explain what a vision-language model does."
```

For an image, set the path to your own RGB PNG or JPEG. For PDFs, render pages to images first:

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
./llama.cpp/llama-mtmd-cli \
    --model "$MODEL_FILE" --mmproj "$MMPROJ_FILE" \
    --ctx-size 16384 --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 0 --min-p 0.0 \
    --image /path/to/picture.jpg \
    --prompt "Describe this image and extract any visible text."
```

4

**Run video**

Start the multimodal CLI:

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
./llama.cpp/llama-mtmd-cli \
    --model "$MODEL_FILE" --mmproj "$MMPROJ_FILE" \
    --ctx-size 16384 --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 0 --min-p 0.0
```

Then enter these lines **inside the CLI**:

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
/video /path/to/video.mp4
Summarize the video and describe the key events.
```

The model card recommends **MP4 clips of 1–2 minutes**. NIM samples at 2 FPS, up to 256 frames; local sampling depends on the runtime. Start with a short clip and increase context as needed, since video frames consume prompt tokens.

#### Llama-server serving and deployment[Direct link to heading](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/nemotron-3.5-super-vl\#llama-server-serving-and-deployment)

1

**Start llama-server**

Create a media directory and start the server:

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
mkdir -p media
./llama.cpp/llama-server \
    --model "$MODEL_FILE" --mmproj "$MMPROJ_FILE" \
    --alias nemotron-super-vl \
    --ctx-size 16384 --parallel 1 --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 0 --min-p 0.0 \
    --media-path "$PWD/media" \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:8001** on the same machine to chat with the llama.cpp server.

2

**Send an API request**

For video, copy a short clip to `media/clip.mp4`, then run this command in another terminal:

GitBook AssistantAskCopy

```
curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{
      "model": "nemotron-super-vl",
      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [\
        {"type": "text", "text": "Summarize this video."},\
        {"type": "input_video", "input_video": {"url": "file://clip.mp4"}}\
      ]}],
      "max_tokens": 1024
    }'
```

`--media-path` allows the server to read local media from that directory. For text-only requests, use `"content": "What is 2+2?"` instead of the content array.
